record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set, diffeomorphic to R3, that contains an apparent horizon?

evidence.quote: Prove there is an AF vacuum initial data set, diffeomorphic to R3, which contains an apparent horizon.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations consist of a triple $(M, g, K)$, where $M$ is a smooth 3-manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $M$, satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R(g)$ denotes the scalar curvature of $g$. The data set $(M,g,K)$ is called asymptotically flat if there exists a compact set $C \subset M$ and a diffeomorphism from $M \setminus C$ to the complement of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ in which, in the standard Euclidean coordinates $x^i$,
$$g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-\alpha}), \quad K_{ij} = O(|x|^{-\alpha-1}),$$
together with appropriate decay of derivatives, for some $\alpha>1/2$, and with suitable integrability of the scalar curvature.

For a smooth two-sided closed surface $\Sigma \subset M$ with unit outward normal $\nu$, define the future outgoing null expansion
$$\theta_+(\Sigma) = H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K,$$
where $H_\Sigma$ is the mean curvature of $\Sigma$ with respect to $\nu$ and $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ is the trace of $K$ over $\Sigma$. The surface $\Sigma$ is called a marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) if $\theta_+(\Sigma) = 0$, and the data set is said to contain an apparent horizon if it admits such a (nonempty) MOTS.

Question: Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set $(M, g, K)$ with $M$ diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ that contains an apparent horizon?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface various constructions of asymptotically flat vacuum initial data and of apparent horizons (e.g., gluing constructions of Corvino–Schoen and Chruściel–Mazzeo, scalar-flat metrics on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with minimal spheres), but no source clearly establishes or refutes the existence of an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set on a manifold diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ that contains an apparent horizon. The problem appears in compilations of open problems in mathematical relativity, and no definitive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: A note on asymptotically flat metrics on R^3 which are scalar-flat and admit minimal spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of asymptotically flat scalar-flat metrics on R^3 admitting minimal spheres.
status_evidence.claim: In the time-symmetric (K=0) vacuum setting, existence of such metrics on R^3 with minimal spheres is known; the general (non-time-symmetric) vacuum case is more delicate.

status_evidence.title: Initial Data Engineering (Chruściel–Isenberg–Pollack)
status_evidence.snippet: Gluing constructions producing vacuum initial data with Schwarzschild ends near horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Gluing methods yield vacuum data with apparent horizons but typically introduce additional asymptotic ends, so they do not immediately give data on R^3.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical General Relativity: A Sampler
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of mathematical general relativity including discussion of MOTS and apparent horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context but does not resolve existence of vacuum AF data on R^3 with an apparent horizon.
